logline: A police academy student moonlights as a masked vigilante executing criminals who escaped justice, until an obsessive investigator and a relentless reporter close in on his double life.

bollymeter.basis: Strong Nam Joo-hyuk lead and bold vigilante-justice premise earn broad goodwill; compressed pacing in the final stretch is the main knock per audience and reviewer consensus. IMDb 7.7 and MyDramaList 8.5 from over 28,000 users reflect a passionate fanbase.

seasons.review_body: Eight episodes dropped across November 2023 on Disney+, adapting Kim Gyu-sam's Naver webtoon with enough conviction to break beyond the usual K-drama lane. Nam Joo-hyuk plays a police cadet who quietly kills the criminals the courts release, delivering physical restraint and moral ambiguity. Yoo Ji-tae's cat-and-mouse detective work sharpens the structure and sustains tension. The premise stays gripping, and the lead performance feels revelatory, but eight episodes prove too compact for the ethical weight the show sets up. Nominated for Outstanding Korean Drama at the 2024 Seoul International Drama Awards. A season 2 now in production suggests the story found its audience.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Vigilante Season 1 Episode 1 aired November 8, 2023 on Disney+. The series holds 7.7 on IMDb and 8.5 on MyDramaList from over 28,000 users; it was nominated for Outstanding Korean Drama at the 2024 Seoul International Drama Awards. The premiere establishes the show's psychological grammar immediately: a top-ranking police academy student who moonlights as an extrajudicial executioner, with no comedic framing or superhero mythology to cushion the moral proposition. Nam Joo-hyuk's physicality communicates Kim Ji-yong's controlled discipline - a performance calibrated to suggest a man whose violence feels like a logical extension of his academic precision rather than a break from it. The cold open positions the show as a psychological pressure cooker rather than a vigilante power fantasy, and Yoo Ji-tae's introduction as the investigator closing in on Ji-yong establishes the cat-and-mouse structure the season sustains.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the show's brutal moral logic fast: a police academy top-student who takes extrajudicial action against repeat offenders. The cold open sets a darker, more procedurally grounded tone than typical vigilante dramaland fare.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The opening sequence where Kim Ji-yong makes his first kill signals this will not be a superhero fantasy but a psychological pressure cooker.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 8
episode_reviews.review_body: Vigilante Season 1 Episode 8 aired November 29, 2023 on Disney+ as the series finale. The series holds 7.7 on IMDb and 8.5 on MyDramaList from over 28,000 users; Season 2 was confirmed in production in July 2024 with the principal cast set to return. The finale delivers the central confrontation between Ji-yong and investigator Jo Heon that the season's structure built toward, and it refuses the clean moral verdict that genre convention would supply. The 7.2 bollymeter reflects a finale that executed its narrative task while leaving the ethical questions about vigilante justice open enough to fuel renewed demand from an audience that responded strongly enough to secure a continuation. The ambiguity is the episode's correct creative choice and the series' most honest statement about the premise.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers on its central confrontation but left audience and critics split on whether the season resolved its ethical questions or simply deferred them to a future season. The ambiguous ending fuelled the demand for a confirmed season 2.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final standoff between Ji-yong and investigator Jo Heon, where the show refuses to deliver a clean moral verdict.
